column1: # Sub-agent usage log. TSV so it can be analysed later for patterns:
#   which KINDS of sub-agent task cost how much of a usage window.
# usage_pct_* are read off the UI by Jon - agents cannot see them. "?" = not recorded.
# subagent_tokens / tool_uses / duration_ms come from the task-notification.
# Append one row per sub-agent. Never rewrite history.
# UNCERTAINTY MARKERS on usage_start / usage_end / usage_delta:
#   (no marker) = read cleanly at the right moment. Trust it.
#   ~           = APPROXIMATE. The reading was taken late or early, so the figure
#                 includes work either side of the agent and is BIGGER than the truth.
#                 Treat as an upper bound, not a measurement.
#   ?           = not captured at all.
# ACCURACY MARKERS on usage_start / usage_end / usage_delta:
#   (no marker) = read cleanly right before the agent started and right after it finished.
#   *           = LOW ACCURACY. The reading was taken late, so the window includes work
#                 other than the agent's - director activity before or after it. The true
#                 cost of the agent is SMALLER than the number shown. Do not treat starred
#                 rows as comparable to clean ones when looking for patterns.
#   ?           = not captured at all. Blank by design, not an error.
# FROM 2026-09-26 (local, branch feature/local-cloud-code-homebrew):
#   agent_type records the model too: general-purpose/opus or general-purpose/sonnet.
#   Every row gets subagent_tokens, tool_uses and duration_ms from the completion notice.
#   Kinds added: research (now includes the bank check), write-prose (2 writers a chapter, own
#   gap research), check (sonnet checker), check-calibration (opus twin of a checker run),
#   fix (opus fixer), gaps (round 2), salvage-read (sonnet).
#   The cloud rows above (2026-09-26, [CLOUD]) are the baseline this run is compared against.

column1: # FINDING UPDATED (2026-09-07) - THE 12,000-TOKENS-PER-POINT RULE IS FALSIFIED.
# T-209: 204,654 subagent tokens for 29% of a window = 7,057 tokens/pt, roughly HALF
# the rate of the four runs it was derived from. subagent_tokens alone does NOT predict
# window cost. Do not size tasks off tok/pt.
#   run    tokens    tools  duration  %     tok/pt
# The four cheap runs were all VERIFY tasks (read + reason, few writes). T-209 was the
# first FIX task: many edits, many re-reads, 109 tool calls, 16.6 minutes. Working
# hypothesis: cost tracks DURATION and TOOL CALLS - the agent's whole context is re-sent
# every turn - more than it tracks the reported token total. Needs more fix-type rows.
# MARKER LEGEND, EXTENDED 2026-09-07
#   (none) = read cleanly at the right moment. Trust it.
#   ~      = APPROXIMATE. Taken late or early. Treat the delta as an UPPER BOUND.
#   +      = CONTAMINATED BY DIRECTOR WORK. The window between the two readings
#            contains work the DIRECTOR did before or after the agent ran, not just
#            the agent. The agent's own share is LOWER, by an unknown amount.
#   ?      = not captured.
# T-209 is marked + . Jon's correction, 2026-09-07: "the fact that you did lots of
# stuff after the agent finished, which I included in that one, decreases the accuracy
# of the last one you did." Between the 38% and 67% readings the director also ran
# four grep sweeps, wrote two long WORKLOG blocks, read three sections of
# project_state.py, wrote a 140-line patch script, and put a two-part question to Jon.
# So 29% is the cost of THAT WHOLE STRETCH, not the cost of the fix agent.
# RULE GOING FORWARD: a clean reading brackets the agent and nothing else. If director
# work falls inside the bracket, mark the row + and do not use it for sizing.
# TASK CATEGORIES - use one of these in the `kind` column, every row.
# Jon's instruction, 2026-09-07: categorize what agents DO, so cost correlates with
# a KIND of work rather than being averaged across unlike tasks.
#   research     web-heavy discovery; writes research/research-<slug>.md + outline.
#                Many fetches, long duration. No prior file to read.
#   write-prose  produces manuscript/<slug>/*.md from an existing outline + bank.
#                Reads 2 files deeply, writes one long one.
#   verify       reads and judges; REPORTS ONLY, writes nothing. Cheapest kind
#                observed (T-206/207/208: 9-14% each, 18-38 tool calls).
#   fix          edits existing files to close named defects. Many small reads and
#                edits; tool-call count is the cost driver, not word count.
#   audit        sweeps many files for a pattern. Untested as an agent task; the
#                director can do the mechanical part with grep for ~0.
#   tooling      changes to scripts in tools/. Usually director work, not an agent.
# What the five rows so far actually say:
#   verify x4  ->  9%, ~12%, 13%, 14%    (113k-167k tokens, 18-51 tool calls)
#   fix   x1   ->  29+% (contaminated; true figure unknown and lower)
# There is NO clean fix-type row yet, and no research or write-prose row measured
# under the bracketing rule above. Do not size anything off this table until each
# category has at least two clean rows.
